h1:
Chanthaburi Riverside Community
Old Wooden Houses, Cafes & Riverside Eats
intro: The Chanthaburi Riverside Community is an old-town quarter along the Chanthaburi River that's been here for more than 100 years. It was originally called "Ban Lum," the place where Chinese and Vietnamese traders settled to do business back in the early Rattanakosin era. Today the old wooden shophouses lining both sides of the narrow lane are still lived in for real. Some have opened as cafes, souvenir shops, small galleries, and noodle stalls passed down through generations. You can easily spend the whole day here, eating and snapping photos as you go.

blocks.html: If you're in Chanthaburi with half a day to a full day to spare, the Riverside Community is where a lot of people start. The area isn't big — the main walkway is a lane running along the river for about 1 kilometer, and walking from one end to the other doesn't take long. But once you stop for coffee, stop for noodles, stop to photograph the wooden houses, a whole afternoon can disappear without you noticing. The charm here is that it's still a community where people actually live, not a set built for tourists.

blocks.text: What's in the area and how to walk it

blocks.html: The community stretches along the west bank of the Chanthaburi River, with a small bridge crossing to the church side. The main walkway is a narrow concrete road flanked by wooden shophouses and old masonry buildings on both sides. Some stretches open up to a clear river view; others are shaded, tucked-away lanes. Popular stops include historic houses, cafes, food spots, and riverside photo corners.

items: Luang Rajamaitri House — A historic wooden house around 150 years old, converted into a hotel and museum telling the story of Luang Rajamaitri, the pioneer who brought rubber tree cultivation to eastern Thailand. The ground floor is open to visitors, and it earned a UNESCO conservation award.
Riverside walking street — The community's main walkway, lined with restaurants, sweet shops, cafes, traditional Chinese pharmacies, and antique stores.
River bridge to the church side — Walk across to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, an old Catholic church on the opposite bank that connects on foot.
Riverside corners — Many shops have seating facing the river. In the late afternoon, with the sun softening and a cool breeze, it's a chill spot where locals come too.

blocks.title: Which day to walk it
blocks.html: Saturday and Sunday are when the most shops are open and the atmosphere is liveliest. On weekdays it's quieter, with only some shops open — good for anyone who wants to photograph the old houses without the crowds. Pick whichever style suits you.

blocks.text: Local eats you have to try

blocks.html: Food is the main reason people stop by the Riverside Community — from Sen Chan noodles, the town's signature dish, to old-style sweets and cold ma-pid (calamansi) juice. We've picked out the shops and dishes you can find in this quarter and nearby.

items.name: Sen Chan Noodles
items.blurb: Soft, chewy rice noodles that are Chanthaburi's signature. You can have them stir-fried with crab or in soup. Plenty of shops in the quarter and around town serve them, and it's the first dish people come to Chanthaburi intending to try.

items.name: Pa Mai Kuay Jab
items.blurb: Thick-broth kuay jab simmered with fragrant bones into a well-rounded flavor. It's an old shop that locals in the quarter keep recommending to one another.

items.name: Je Eed Seafood Tom Yum Noodles
items.blurb: A bold, well-seasoned tom yum — sour, salty, sweet, and spicy in true Chanthaburi style — served with fresh seafood. Great for anyone who loves big flavors.

items.name: Ban Chan Dee Boat Noodles
items.blurb: A shop set in a vintage old wooden house by the river. You choose your noodles and toppings — fresh pork, braised pork, meatballs — and can add an onsen egg. Seating on both sides of the road, and it photographs beautifully.
items.meta: Lunch · small bowls start in the single digits

items.name: Pad Thai 100 Krata
items.blurb: An old-style pad thai shop with a yellow roadside sign and wooden tables under a wide roof. The same familiar hand-cooked taste people keep coming back for.

items.name: Ma-pid Juice (Calamansi Juice)
items.blurb: A local drink made from Chanthaburi's calamansi, with a refreshing sweet-sour taste that's easy to drink. You can buy a bottle to take home as a gift too.

items.name: Khanom Khai & Traditional Sweets
items.blurb: Along the lanes are several shops making traditional sweets fresh — khanom khai, khanom jeeb, and Chanthaburi-style khanom jeen. Easy to grab and snack on as you walk.

items.name: Rocket Ice Cream
items.blurb: A retro Thai ice cream shop, easy to spot by its big rocket logo. It offers a range of Thai-style flavors — perfect for beating the midday heat.

blocks.title: Lunch tip
blocks.html: The popular noodle shops often sell out by mid-afternoon. If you're set on Sen Chan noodles or an old-school kuay jab shop, start your meal before 1 PM, then hit the cafes in the afternoon — you'll get the full lineup.

In the past few years, many of the old wooden shophouses have been turned into small cafes that keep the original house structure intact, so you get to sip coffee in a genuinely old-house setting. Some shops face their seating toward the river, and the late afternoon, with softer sun and a cool breeze, hits just right.

items.name: Sukjai
items.blurb: A small cafe in the community, decorated in warm, mellow tones with plenty of photo corners. Open roughly 08:00–18:00.

items.name: Rock S'Presso
items.blurb: A coffee shop known for its big espresso machine, with coffee and desserts to choose from, plus food.

items.name: TEIM
items.blurb: A cafe in the quarter that reviewers have mentioned often in recent years. Relaxed atmosphere, good for a rest while you're walking.

items.name: Riverside cafes in old houses
items.blurb: Several shops along the lane have seating facing the river, ideal for the late afternoon to watch the boats and riverside life.

blocks.text: How to get there · where to park

blocks.html: The Chanthaburi Riverside Community sits in the center of Mueang Chanthaburi district and is easy to reach. Driving from Bangkok, take Sukhumvit Road toward Chanthaburi — it takes about 3.5–4 hours. The lane itself is narrow and awkward for cars, so most people park on the outside and walk in.

items: Park at a nearby temple — Park at Wat Chantanaram or the temple/church-side lot, which has plenty of space, then walk across the bridge into the community.
Affordable parking — Some spots charge around 20 THB for all day.
Time for the visit — Allow about 1–3 hours to walk, eat, and take photos. If you linger long at a cafe, you can easily spend half a day.
Come morning to afternoon — Restaurants open at midday and cafes stay open until evening. In the late afternoon the soft light is great for riverside photos.

blocks.text: A full-day walking plan in the old town

blocks.html: If you want to cover the Riverside Community in full — the food, the cafes, and the old houses — try laying out the day like this, adjusting the timing to your own pace.

blocks.label: Morning half
blocks.title: Start with food and a historic house

items.activity: Park on the temple side, walk across the bridge into the community, and start at the top of the lane
items.note: Early on there are still few people, so you can photograph the wooden houses nicely

items.activity: Stop for a late-morning meal with kuay jab or Sen Chan noodles at an old shop in the quarter
items.note: Popular shops sell out fast — arriving before noon is the safer bet

items.activity: Visit Luang Rajamaitri House and hear the community's story and the history of rubber
items.note: The ground floor is a small museum open to visitors

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.title: Cafes, souvenirs, and the church across the river

items.activity: Walk and sample traditional sweets along the lanes, and grab a cold ma-pid juice
items.note: Souvenirs keep well — buy some to take home

items.activity: Sit at a riverside cafe, rest your legs, and sip coffee while watching life along the river
items.note: Pick a shop with seating facing the water

items.activity: Walk across the bridge to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
items.note: An old Catholic church you can reach on foot from the community

items.activity: Come back to catch the riverside photo corners in the soft light, and finish with ice cream or a dessert
items.note: The evening light makes for the best photos of the day

blocks.title: Want to extend the trip
blocks.html: If you still have energy, drive on from the Riverside Community to the Chanthaburi Gem Market on the weekend, or save a nature spot like Phlio Waterfall for the next day. Chanthaburi packs an old town, the sea, and the mountains into one province.

faq.q: What days and hours is the Chanthaburi Riverside Community open?
faq.a: You can walk it any day, but the most shops are open on Saturday and Sunday. Most restaurants open at midday, and many cafes open around 08:00–18:00. Weekdays are quieter with only some shops open — good for anyone who wants to photograph the old houses in peace.

faq.q: How long does it take to visit the Chanthaburi Riverside Community?
faq.a: If you just walk around looking at the old houses and taking photos, it takes about 1–2 hours. But if you stop for noodles, sit at a cafe, and cross over to see the church on the other side too, you can easily spend half a day to a full day.

faq.q: What food should you try at the Riverside Community?
faq.a: Sen Chan noodles are the number-one signature, followed by old-school kuay jab, bold seafood tom yum, an old-school pad thai shop, traditional sweets, and cold calamansi (ma-pid) juice that you can buy as a souvenir.

faq.q: Where do you park when visiting the Chanthaburi Riverside Community?
faq.a: The lanes in the community are narrow and awkward for cars, so people usually park at a nearby temple lot like Wat Chantanaram or on the church side, then walk across the bridge in. Some spots charge around 20 THB for all day.

faq.q: First time in Chanthaburi — should you start at the Riverside Community?
faq.a: It's a great fit, since it's right in the center of town and brings together old houses, local food, cafes, and the church in one spot. You can walk it comfortably in half a day, then move on to the gem market, the sea, or a waterfall the next day.
